detector_gaps_found: SCRIPT_RE = r"scripts/[A-Za-z0-9_\-./]+\.(?:py|sh|js|ts)" has no boundary after the extension, so `scripts/chron_events.json` matches as `scripts/chron_events.js` (the `.js` alternative fires and `on` is left over). This produced the alpha-zen-lanes finding.

The `/foo|bar|baz|...` documented-example guard is applied only inside the PATH_RE loop (line ~86), never inside the SCRIPT_RE loop — so `scripts/foo.sh` (hermes-cron-zen) and `scripts/foo.py` (skill-library-integrity) are reported although they are textbook illustration names.

DEAD-PATH reporting is existence-only and not negation-aware (only the IMMUTABLE test checks NEGATION), so a body that correctly marks a path as gone/UNBUILT keeps being re-reported. This is why the doctrine-sealing 'never write it' line still surfaces.
